title: Slow Cooker Chickpea & Potato Stew
description: A mild, filling crockpot stew built from chickpeas, potatoes, tomatoes, and everyday seasonings.
substitutions: Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Add 2 cups chopped cabbage during the final hour if you have some to use up.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a little stew to thicken and serve.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 cans chickpeas, 4 cups diced potatoes, 1 can diced tomatoes, 3 cups broth, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1/2 teaspoon thyme, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a few potato and chickpea pieces against the side of the cooker, stir, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Garlic Cabbage & Potatoes
description: Crisp-edged cabbage and tender potatoes turn two inexpensive staples into an easy sheet-pan side or light meal.
substitutions: Use sweet potatoes for half of the white potatoes.
Sprinkle with Parmesan after roasting if desired.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 4 cups chopped cabbage and 3 cups diced potatoes with 2 tablespoons oil, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Spread on a large sheet pan and roast 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and the cabbage has browned edges.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven, air fryer, or skillet for the best texture.

title: Leftover Chicken & Rice Soup
description: A quick soup that turns cooked chicken and cooked rice into another warm meal without tasting like leftovers.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of chicken.
Use cooked noodles instead of rice and add them only for the final few minutes.

steps.text: Add chicken and rice and heat through.

cookSteps.text: Combine 5 cups chicken broth, 1 cup frozen mixed vegetables, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon thyme, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in 2 cups cooked chicken and 1 1/2 cups cooked rice. Simmer 5–7 minutes until everything is hot.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. The rice will absorb broth, so add extra broth or water when reheating.

title: Small-Batch Peanut Butter Blondies
description: A small pan of soft peanut-butter bars for when you want something sweet without making a full-size dessert.
substitutions: Use smooth or crunchy peanut butter.
Fold in 2 tablespoons chocolate chips if you have them.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease an 8x4-inch loaf pan.
Stir together 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1 egg, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla until smooth. Stir in 1/4 cup flour and 1/4 teaspoon baking powder just until combined.
Spread the batter in the pan and bake 18–20 minutes, until the center is set but still soft.
Cool at least 10 minutes before cutting into 6 small bars.

storage: Store covered at room temperature up to 3 days or refrigerate up to 5 days.
